slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content: Côtes d'Auvergne — Volcanic Terroir Gems — This course covers Côtes-d'Auvergne, Côtes-d'Auvergne-Boudes, Côtes-d'Auvergne-Chateaugay, Côtes-d'Auvergne-Corent, and Côtes-d'Auvergne-Madargues, exploring the unique volcanic terroir of the Loire Valley's southernmost quality wine region.
slides.1.title: Côtes d'Auvergne — Volcanic Terroir Gems
slides.1.content:
This course systematically explores the terroir characteristics of Côtes-d'Auvergne, Côtes-d'Auvergne-Boudes, Côtes-d'Auvergne-Chateaugay, Côtes-d'Auvergne-Corent, and Côtes-d'Auvergne-Madargues, helping you build a solid knowledge framework for the Loire Valley. Located in the Massif Central, these volcanic-soil wines represent a completely different character from the rest of the Loire.

Through systematic study, you will be able to identify the typical styles of these AOCs and accurately describe their characteristics during tasting.
slides.2.title: Quiz
slides.2.questions.0.question: Which of the following AOCs is covered in this course?
slides.2.questions.0.explanation: Côtes-d'Auvergne is an important AOC in the Loire Valley and a core subject of this course. Located in the Massif Central (Puy-de-Dôme department), it produces primarily Gamay and Pinot Noir reds/rosés on volcanic basalt and granite soils. Its five named crus — Boudes, Chateaugay, Corent, Madargues, and Châteaumeillant — each have distinct volcanic terroir characteristics.
